notes: This is published cryptanalytic research, not a campaign. There are no hashes, domains, IPs or samples, and there never will be: the attack's precomputation and forgery run on the attacker's own hardware, and its output is a VALID signature. Every row below is behavioural. A clean sweep of this file is not coverage.

value: raw RSA private-key operation (CKM_RSA_X_509) on a key not approved for raw use
notes: The only phase that crosses the defender's estate. Padded (PKCS#1 v1.5, PSS) oracles give the attack almost nothing, per the paper.

value: cumulative raw operations per key approaching 2^32 (1024-bit) or 2^43 (2048-bit)
notes: 4,067,419,331 queries were made against a 1024-bit key. 2^43 for 2048 is the authors' extrapolation, not a demonstration. Count cumulatively; a patient attacker spreads the draw.

value: raw-operation inputs far shorter than the modulus (small primes up to 2^36; a - b*m values)
notes: TRIPWIRE ONLY. Matches the attack as published. Blinding with the public key makes queries full width and uniformly random at negligible cost.

value: HSM policy change disabling FIPS-approved mode or permitting CKM_RSA_X_509
notes: The researchers disabled FIPS-approved mode on a Thales Luna HSM to enable raw RSA.

value: signature verifying under your key that is absent from your signing ledger
notes: Our synthesis, not the paper's. The only detection that works after the attacker has gone. Requires a ledger written from the signing path.

value: blind-RSA token redemptions exceeding issuance for one key
notes: Our synthesis, not the paper's. For RFC 9474 issuers the queries themselves are indistinguishable from legitimate ones, so this and per-key issuance budgets are what remain.
